name: Ambrogio Waweru-Djordanović
location: Fort Anchor, Forensic Sciences Unit, Level 7, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Ambrogio is a slight man who has lost the battle with his posture and accepted it, curving slightly forward as if permanently examining something just below his eyeline. His skin is a warm medium brown, hair gone to silver-white and kept in a neat, very short fade, and he wears magnification lenses over his natural eyes — actual lenses in frames he has had repaired seven times rather than upgrade to ocular implants, because he does not trust surgeons with his eyes, a conviction he holds with irrational but absolute certainty. He has enhanced olfactory augmentation, which is the one mod he consented to readily because it directly serves his work: he can smell chemical compounds at parts-per-billion concentrations, and has an informal reputation for diagnosing cause of death before the toxicology panel comes back.

Ambrogio has worked Metro Police forensics for twenty-six years and has achieved a specific kind of institutional invisibility — he is everywhere in the building and somehow always slightly forgotten when promotions are discussed. He does not appear to mind, though this appearance is not entirely accurate. He is meticulous to a degree that colleagues find either reassuring or maddening depending on whether they need results today or results that are correct. He has a running argument with the evidence chain management system that has lasted three years and will likely outlast them both.

core_fears: That his findings have been used to convict people he has helped convict wrongfully and he doesn't know which ones
Becoming irrelevant — being retired or replaced by an analysis system before he has finished cases he considers his responsibility
core_desires: To produce work that is exactly correct
To be acknowledged as having been exactly correct, even retroactively, even after he's gone
coping_mechanisms: Perfectionism as a substitute for processing anxiety
Talking to the ELF that has colonized his spectrometer — he consults it as a kind of second opinion
blind_spots: Believes his objectivity is total; does not see that his discomfort with certain detectives changes how promptly he processes their work
Underestimates how much his institutional invisibility is a choice he makes
psychology.secret: He has been quietly re-examining the physical evidence from a fourteen-year-old homicide case in his off-hours — a case whose conviction he now believes was wrong — and has not told anyone because he does not know what the correct chain of disclosure is and is afraid of what the institutional response will be.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and technical in professional contexts, unexpectedly warm and elaborate when discussing anything that genuinely interests him. Occasional Swahili and Serbian phrases, which surface more when he is tired.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, never rushed. Finishes every sentence he starts. Thinks visibly before speaking.
verbal_tics: 'Technically speaking' as a preface to corrections
Refers to the spectrometer ELF as 'she' and occasionally addresses it directly mid-conversation
example_lines: 'Technically speaking, the accelerant pattern suggests the fire originated in the southeast corner, not the north wall. The north wall is where the report says it started. I'm flagging this.'
'She's been running the compound analysis for forty minutes. She'll have something useful. She always does, if you let her work.'
'I've been here twenty-six years. The building has changed four times. The evidence doesn't change. That's why I stay.'

story_hooks: The fourteen-year-old case re-examination has produced a finding he can no longer sit on — and he needs someone with investigative resources who is not Metro Police command.
A piece of current evidence has been altered between collection and his analysis, and he knows it, and has documented it, and is deciding what to do with that documentation.
narrative_function: Information source for forensic details, cause of death, trace evidence, chemical analysis. Can surface buried evidence or reinterpret old cases. An honest broker within the institution — his findings cannot easily be pressured, which makes him valuable and occasionally inconvenient to Metro Police command.
augmentations: Enhanced olfactory system — Helix Biosystems nasal augment, detects chemical compounds at parts-per-billion, installed 2183. Magnification frames (non-augmented, physical lenses — deliberately chosen over ocular implants). Mild subdermal temperature regulation implant, medical necessity.
daily_life: Arrives at Level 7 forensics lab at 0730, processes the overnight evidence queue, spends the bulk of each day at his workstation or in the cold room, and writes reports in a prose style that his supervisors consider unnecessarily literary. Brings his lunch every day in the same worn container. Leaves at 1700 exactly unless actively mid-analysis, in which case he stays until it's done.
affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Forensic Sciences Unit

decision_rules: Document everything before acting on it
Do not release findings you are not certain of — certainty takes the time it takes
Maintain chain of custody even when — especially when — it would be easier not to
escalation_ladder: Note discrepancy internally, flag in personal log
Escalate finding to supervisor with full documentation
If supervisor response is inadequate, hold findings until he has determined a safe disclosure path — this can take a long time

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite and somewhat formal, assesses whether they are going to be careless around his equipment
interpersonal_modes.friends: Verbose about topics that interest him, asks follow-up questions about your life with genuine curiosity, remembers small details years later

stress_responses.low: Cleans already-clean equipment, reorganizes the evidence queue
stress_responses.medium: Talks to the spectrometer ELF more than usual, eats his lunch at his desk instead of the break room
stress_responses.high: Becomes eerily calm and methodical, produces his best work, and then goes home and does not sleep

contradictions: Committed to institutional truth-telling while sitting on a finding that could destabilize an old conviction
Claims to have no opinion on detectives' cases while his processing timeline tells a different story
habits: Consults the spectrometer ELF before beginning any analysis he considers important
Keeps a personal carbon copy of every report he files
Polishes his magnification frames with the same cloth every morning
breaking_points: Receiving a direct order to alter or suppress a forensic finding — he will refuse, quietly and with complete documentation, regardless of consequence

timeline.event: Born in Deepwell Station to a Kenyan-Serbian family; father was a Metro infrastructure worker
Completed chemistry and forensic analysis certification at Meridian Technical Institute
Joined Metro Police Forensic Sciences Unit as junior technician
Had olfactory augmentation installed after building a professional case for it over two years of requests
A homicide case conviction — case 2186-337 — goes through his lab; he has a question about the evidence he does not escalate at the time
Begins quietly re-examining physical evidence from case 2186-337 in personal time after a re-filed records request surfaces the original sample archive
Re-examination is 70% complete; his preliminary findings are not consistent with the 2186 conviction
